item.title: Trump’s Federal School Voucher Plan Has a Big Surprise
item.description: Whether on purpose or by accident, the Trump administration’s new voucher program could do something it never promised to do: help public schools. It’s a bit of a surprise from the White House that promised to abolish the Department of Education and then dismantled large parts of it. But under rules released this month by the US Treasury Department, the program authorizing the first Federal Scholarship Tax Credit allows kids to receive a voucher even if they stay in their public school.
item.dc:creator: Mary Ellen Klas

item.title: Aaron Sorkin Got The Social Reckoning Half Right
item.description: As fate would have it, the sequel to The Social Network is almost as beleaguered as Facebook itself. The Social Reckoning, which dramatizes the 2021 leak that led to The Wall Street Journal’s 17-part investigative series into the platform, had a lukewarm critical reception and tepid opening weekend at the box office, grossing just $5.5 million domestically. The response is a far cry from The Social Network, the 2010 drama that won three Oscars and ended up grossing nearly $225 million.
item.dc:creator: Miles Surrey

item.title: Russia’s Claim to Ukraine Is an Existential Crisis for Putin and Strongmen
item.description: The president and his allies genuinely believe the creation of Ukraine required ripping out Russia’s historic heartland.
item.dc:creator: Brooke Sample

item.title: Sally Rooney Book Withdrawal Is Absurd. Palestine Action Is Not a Terror Group
item.description: If Fyodor Dostoevsky were alive today he would be appearing on Russia Today to cheer on Vladimir Putin’s invasion of Ukraine. The author of The Brothers Karamazov, Crime and Punishment and other great works of the literary canon was also prone to anti-Semitic outbursts and was vitriolic in his denunciation of the Roman Catholic church, nineteenth-century Western liberals and their Russian admirers who wanted to reform his beloved Tsarist autocracy.
item.dc:creator: Martin Ivens
